web_title: 6. Multi-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Capital Structure
book_title: Chapter 6: The Forensic Ledger — 5-Year Financials, Cash & Dilution
question: Do Yash Highvoltage's 5-year P&L, balance sheet, cash conversion, return ratios, and equity raises hold up under forensic scrutiny?

epigraph.quote: Rapid revenue growth funded by equity is easy to admire; the forensic question is whether incremental capital earns its keep once the working-capital tide settles.
epigraph.author: Financial Forensics Principle

web_blocks.html: Between FY22 and FY26, Yash compounded revenue at ~38% CAGR, from ₹65.06 crore to ₹235.1 crore [1][10]. Over that same span, PAT compounded at ~44% CAGR from ₹8.71 crore to ₹37.4 crore [1][10]. Growth sped up in H1 FY27, with revenue up 95% YoY to ₹194.5 crore [1][3]. EBITDA surged 136% YoY to ₹54.7 crore (28.1% margin) [1][3]. PAT jumped 165% YoY to ₹36.2 crore (18.6% margin), nearly matching full-year FY26 PAT in six months [1][3].

web_blocks.caption: 5-Year Financial Forensics Summary (FY22–FY26 & H1 FY27, ₹ Crore)
web_blocks.takeaway: Gross margin expanded +800 bps from FY24 (40.3%) to H1 FY27 (48.3%) via RIP mix & operating leverage; H1 FY27 CFO surged to ₹45.2 Cr (125% of PAT). *FY22–FY23 EBITDA figures reflect DRHP pre-Ind AS disclosures; FY26 EBITDA of ₹60.4 Cr includes ₹5.8 Cr other income [1][10].

web_blocks.title: 6.2 Cash Conversion, Working Capital & Balance Sheet Forensics

web_blocks.html: A forensic cash-flow check explains the sole historical blemish in Yash's numbers. From FY22 to FY26, cumulative PAT totaled ~₹91.2 crore against ~₹44.7 crore of cumulative CFO, a ~49% conversion ratio [1][10]. Rapid growth absorbed working capital each year, peaking in FY26 when inventory jumped from ₹29.67 crore to ₹66.65 crore [1][10]. That build left FY26 CFO at ₹8.82 crore against ₹37.4 crore of PAT [1]. H1 FY27 broke that trend cleanly. Inventory rose just ₹5.1 crore to ₹71.8 crore on nearly doubled revenue [1]. Trade payables and customer advances grew, pushing CFO to ₹45.2 crore (125% of PAT) [1].

Total debt peaked at ₹31.09 crore in March 2026 (0.17x D/E) and fell to ₹10.30 crore by September 2026 (₹5.4 Cr long-term; ₹4.9 Cr short-term) [1]. With cash and bank deposits near ₹95.6 crore (net cash ₹95 crore), solvency risk is negligible [1][2]. Return ratios moderated after equity raises expanded net worth from ₹41.73 crore (Mar-24) to ₹319.60 crore (Sep-26) [1]. ROCE moved from 43.6% (FY23) to 25.1% (FY26), while ROE moved from 40.4% to 22.5% [1]. Meanwhile, ₹17.2 crore of CWIP and ₹10.3 crore of intangibles under development await Jarod's ramp [1]. Two FY26 footnotes also merit scrutiny: Yash transitioned from IGAAP to Ind AS for the first time with unmodified audit opinions [7]. It also booked a ₹2.10 crore (₹210.10 lakh) exceptional loss in March/April 2026 after a vendor-impersonation cyber fraud diverted payment to a fraudulent bank account (reported on the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal, with recovery contingent on police investigation) [7].

web_blocks.title: 6.3 Share Dilution, Preferential Issue, Promoter Selling & BSE SME Governance

web_blocks.html: Yash tapped equity markets twice in two years to fund expansion without debt. First, the December 2024 BSE SME IPO raised ~₹70.34 Cr for Jarod plus ₹14.76 Cr for GCP (with ₹9.17 Cr of IPO expenses adjusted against Securities Premium) [1][10]. Second, the June/August 2026 ₹151 crore preferential issue (12.6 lakh shares + 8.3 lakh convertible warrants held by Malabar India Fund over an 18-month exercise window, 25% paid upfront) funded Phase 2 550 kV core capacity, backed by WhiteOak Capital, ValueQuest, Motilal Oswal, and Malabar India Fund [1][6]. On 14 November 2026, Monitoring Agency Acuité Ratings & Research confirmed zero deviation in utilization of those preferential proceeds through September 2026 [33]. On September 30, 2026, Promoters held 53.79% (50.57% fully diluted) with 0.0% pledge, Mutual Funds held 2.45%, AIFs held 7.23%, and the Employee Benefit Trust held 3.36% [6].

However, multi-tranche promoter open-market selling and corporate-structure layering emerged as fresh governance watchpoints during September–November 2026 [34][41]. On 7 September 2026, Promoter Group member Twinkle Keyur Shah sold 248,000 shares (₹23.50 Cr) and Chairman & MD Keyur Shah sold 52,000 shares (₹4.93 Cr) on BSE [41]. Subsequently, per BSE SAST/PIT disclosures filed on 17 November 2026, Keyur Shah sold an additional 100,000 shares across 11 November (50,000 shares, ~₹6.21 Cr) and 13 November (50,000 shares, ~₹6.26 Cr) [34]. Those sales cut his personal stake from 50.58% to 50.24% and brought cumulative Sep–Nov promoter-family open-market disposals to 400,000 shares (~₹40.9 crore), lowering total promoter group ownership to ~53.45% (~50.2% fully diluted) from the September 30 base [6][34][41]. Separately, since FY25 Yash added four new entities—including non-consolidated Section 8 CSR subsidiary Abhigam Foundation (controlled by Keyur Shah), Yash HV USA Inc., Yash HV Power Components Pvt. Ltd., and the 50% Sukrut Electric JV [7]. It also extended ESOP 2025 exercise periods from 2 to 4 years and allotted 9,200 equity shares on 21 October 2026 (lifting paid-up shares to 2,98,96,880) [9][42]. Finally, because Yash listed on BSE SME on 19 December 2024, BSE's mandatory 3-year SME listing tenure bars Mainboard migration before December 2027, keeping half-yearly reporting and lot-size liquidity constraints [10].

web_blocks.title: Forensic Watchpoints Entering H2 FY27 & FY28
paragraphs: 1. Promoter Open-Market Selling & Dilution Overhang: Promoter-family disposals totaled 400,000 shares (~₹40.9 Cr) across Sep–Nov 2026 (including Keyur Shah's Nov 11–13 sales disclosed Nov 17) [34][41], alongside 8.3 lakh unexercised Malabar warrants (₹60 Cr, 18-month window) and ESOP 2025 allotments [6][42].

2. Internal Controls & Group Structure: March 2026's ₹2.10 Cr vendor-email cyber fraud exposed payment-verification gaps during rapid scaling [7], while four newly added entities (including non-consolidated Section 8 entity Abhigam Foundation) warrant ongoing related-party scrutiny.

3. Receivable Days & Capital Efficiency: DSO rose from 47 days in FY26 to 66 days in H1 FY27 (receivables ₹69.5 Cr) [1][2], while ₹319.6 Cr of equity and ₹114 Cr of remaining Jarod capex require high plant utilization to sustain ROCE above 22–25%.
4. BSE SME Structural Constraints: Half-yearly statutory reporting opacity and lot-size trading friction persist until Yash clears BSE's 3-year SME migration threshold in December 2027 [10].

web_blocks.title: 6.4 Quarterly & Half-Yearly Margin Progression Through H1 FY27

web_blocks.html: Half-yearly results across H1 FY26 → H2 FY26 → H1 FY27 show steady margin expansion, not a one-quarter spike [1]. Revenue climbed from ₹99.59 crore (H1 FY26) to ₹135.5 crore (H2 FY26) and ₹194.5 crore (H1 FY27), up 44% HoH and 95% YoY [1]. Over those three periods, gross margin rose from 42.4% → 45.9% → 48.3% [1]. EBITDA margin expanded from 23.3% → 27.4% → 28.1%, while PAT margin climbed from 13.7% → 17.5% → 18.6% [1].

Basic EPS followed the same upward path even on a larger share count [1]. It rose from ₹4.77 in H1 FY26 to ₹8.31 in H2 FY26 and ₹12.48 in H1 FY27 [1]. Finance costs stayed low at ₹2.4 crore in H1 FY27 (1.2% of revenue, down from 2.2% in H1 FY26) [1]. Short-term debt fell from ₹24.74 crore in March 2026 to ₹4.9 crore in September 2026 [1].

book_paragraphs: Numbers can tell two different stories depending on whether you stop at the income statement or walk down into the cash-flow and balance-sheet footnotes. On the income statement, Yash Highvoltage looks like a textbook industrial compounder: revenue nearly quadrupled from ₹65.06 crore in FY22 to ₹235.1 crore in FY26, and then hit ₹194.5 crore in the first half of FY27 alone. Even better, gross margins expanded by 800 basis points in two and a half years—from 40.3% in FY24 to 48.3% in H1 FY27—as RIP bushings and aftermarket retrofits took a larger share of the mix.

When we walk into the cash-flow statement and governance footnotes, however, we spot two live tensions. First, between FY22 and FY26, Yash generated ₹91.2 crore of cumulative net profit but only ₹44.7 crore of operating cash flow because every revenue surge forced pre-buying of imported RIP cores—most visibly in FY26, when inventory jumped from ₹29.7 crore to ₹66.7 crore and kept CFO at ₹8.82 crore. Second, FY26 footnotes also recorded an unexpected ₹2.10 crore exceptional loss from a vendor-impersonation cyber fraud in March 2026—a reminder that internal financial controls must scale as fast as factory output.

That is why H1 FY27 and November 2026 provide such important forensic checkpoints. On the positive side, inventory barely budged from ₹66.7 crore to ₹71.8 crore while operating cash flow exploded to ₹45.2 crore (125% of PAT), and Acuité Ratings' 14 November 2026 Monitoring Agency Report confirmed zero deviation on the ₹151 crore preferential issue. On the cautionary side, BSE filings through 17 November 2026 revealed cumulative open-market promoter-family sales of 400,000 shares (~₹40.9 crore) between September and November 2026.

book_subsections.title: Balance Sheet Fortification, Promoter Selling & BSE SME Constraints
paragraphs: You also need to account for how Yash financed its expansion—and how insider ownership and exchange structure are evolving. Rather than loading up on debt like the ill-fated power equipment makers of 2012, Keyur Shah raised equity twice: first in the December 2024 BSE SME IPO, and again in August 2026 via a ₹151 crore preferential issue of shares and convertible warrants (8.3 lakh warrants held by Malabar India Fund) to institutional funds. Shareholders' funds swelled from ₹41.7 crore in March 2024 to ₹319.6 crore by September 2026, while total debt fell to ₹10.3 crore against ₹95 crore of net cash, with Acuité Ratings certifying zero proceeds deviation on 14 November 2026.

At the same time, forensic governance discipline requires tracking three realities the headline balance sheet obscures. First, while promoter shares carry zero pledge and remain above 50% fully diluted, promoter-family open-market selling accelerated in late 2026: Twinkle Keyur Shah (248,000 shares, ₹23.50 crore) and Keyur Shah (52,000 shares, ₹4.93 crore) sold on 7 September 2026, followed by Keyur Shah selling another 100,000 shares (~₹12.5 crore) on 11 and 13 November 2026 (disclosed 17 November), trimming his direct stake from 50.58% to 50.24%. Second, since FY25 Yash added four group entities—including non-consolidated Section 8 CSR subsidiary Abhigam Foundation—and extended ESOP 2025 exercise periods from two to four years. Third, Yash remains on the BSE SME platform, which enforces half-yearly statutory reporting, lot-size liquidity friction, and a mandatory three-year SME listing tenure—blocking Mainboard migration until December 2027.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: Pre-funding a ₹220 crore greenfield plant with equity rather than debt is conservative and smart, and zero-deviation certification from Acuité Ratings confirms disciplined capital deployment. Still, repeated promoter open-market sales (~₹40.9 crore in Sep–Nov 2026) and a ₹2.10 crore cyber-wire lapse mean governance deserves active monitoring rather than passive trust.

book_subsections.title: The Half-Yearly Step-Up: Checking Earnings Quality
paragraphs: Whenever a manufacturing company reports a 165% jump in net profit, a forensic analyst immediately checks whether the surge came from other income, lower tax rates, or accounting tricks. Let us run that check on Yash's H1 FY27 numbers.

In H1 FY27, other income actually fell 45% year-on-year from ₹2.0 crore to ₹1.1 crore, while the effective tax rate held steady at roughly 24.4% (₹11.7 crore tax on ₹47.9 crore PBT). The entire profit expansion came from core operations: gross margins climbed from 42.4% to 48.3%, operating leverage compressed employee costs as a percentage of sales, and finance costs barely moved while short-term debt dropped from ₹24.7 crore to ₹4.9 crore, backed by four straight years of unmodified audit opinions through Yash's first-time Ind AS transition.

Combine that clean operating P&L with ₹45.2 crore of operating cash flow and ₹95 crore of net cash on the balance sheet, and the core earnings engine looks genuinely robust—provided receivable days (66 days in Sep-26), payment-verification controls after the March 2026 cyber-fraud loss, and promoter stake stability stay tightly policed.
